sourceRegistry.name: Wildlife Institute of India / ENVIS — Community Reserves (repackaged by Dataful)

sourceRegistry.name: Wildlife Institute of India — National Wildlife Database, protected-area network snapshot

sourceRegistry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change / ENVIS — Marine Protected Areas in India (as on 24 July 2024), repackaged by Dataful
sourceRegistry.note: 132 records across 11 states/UTs, with name, legal designation category, notification year and area where reported. Dataset updated on Dataful 11 December 2025. Contains overlapping entries already classified as national parks, sanctuaries, community or conservation reserves; do not add to the national protected-area total as a separate legal class.

sourceRegistry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change — Marine Protected Areas and Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas
sourceRegistry.note: Government statement reports 130 notified Marine Protected Areas and 106 prioritized Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas. These are different concepts; ICMBAs are not all notified protected areas.

sourceRegistry.name: Ministry of Jal Shakti — State-wise wetland distribution, National Wetland Decadal Change Atlas (2017–18)
sourceRegistry.note: State/UT wetland counts and mapped area reported in the Lok Sabha reply on National Wetland Conservation Programme. The former Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu rows are combined for the present merged UT. This is a historical remote-sensing inventory snapshot, not a current list of individually named wetlands; Ramsar site records remain in the separate Ramsar category.

sourceRegistry.name: National Water Mission, Ministry of Jal Shakti — First Census of Water Bodies dashboard
sourceRegistry.note: State/UT totals shown on the dashboard as per the ongoing First Census of Water Bodies, data as on 27 July 2026. This is a count of water bodies of multiple classes, not a named lake/reservoir inventory. Only listed state/UT entries are populated; unlisted present-day UTs are not assumed to have zero water bodies.

sourceRegistry.name: Central Water Commission — Weekly Bulletin on Live Storage Status of 166 Reservoirs
sourceRegistry.note: Complete named list of 166 CWC-monitored reservoirs transcribed from the region/state-wise table in the weekly bulletin dated 9 April 2026. This represents the CWC-monitored subset, not a complete inventory of all reservoirs in India.

sourceRegistry.name: NRSC — Glacial Lake Atlas of Indian Himalayan River Basins
sourceRegistry.note: Official inventory of 28,043 glacial lakes >=0.25 ha across Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra basins, mapped from 2016–17 satellite data. This is a spatial lake-ID inventory, not a register of individually named lakes; keep distinct from named natural lakes.

sourceRegistry.name: Ministry of Jal Shakti / CWC — Glacial-lake counts from NRSC Glacial Lake Atlas
sourceRegistry.note: PIB reports 681 glacial lakes located in India, state/UT split: Ladakh 179, Jammu and Kashmir 76, Himachal Pradesh 17, Uttarakhand 13, Sikkim 72, Arunachal Pradesh 324. CWC began monitoring 2,843 glacial lakes and water bodies across the wider Himalayan river basins in 2025; the 681 figure is the India-located subset.

sourceRegistry.name: Sribhumi District Administration, Government of Assam — Son Beel

sourceRegistry.name: Nagaon District Administration, Government of Assam — Samaguri Beel

sourceRegistry.name: Assam State Biodiversity Board — Hajong Lake aquatic biodiversity assessment

sourceRegistry.name: Central Water Commission and ISRO/NRSC — River Basin Atlas of India
sourceRegistry.note: Official CWC–ISRO India-WRIS atlas. State/UT basin associations are curated from CWC basin delineations and the atlas basin maps. The atlas distinguishes CWC's 20 basins from India-WRIS's 25-basin/101-sub-basin framework; this dataset uses the atlas's CWC basin names and labels partial state coverage as an association, not full containment.

sourceRegistry.name: Ministry of Tourism — 340 mountain peaks opened for mountaineering/trekking
sourceRegistry.note: Official annexure lists Himachal Pradesh 91, Jammu and Kashmir 133 (including present-day Ladakh), Sikkim 10 and Uttarakhand 106. The 340 annexure entries have not been bulk-imported: its historic J&K/Ladakh administrative split and coded or unnamed summit entries require geospatial reconciliation. Current peak records instead comprise the deduplicated 2019 PIB list, selected 2026 Uttarakhand examples, and separately verified regional peaks.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (4)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Andhra Pradesh: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 4 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Andhra Pradesh: Priority I 0, II 0, III 1, IV 0, V 3. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (6)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Assam: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 6 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Assam: Priority I 1, II 0, III 0, IV 1, V 4. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 12 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Bihar: Priority I 0, II 0, III 4, IV 2, V 6. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 2 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Goa: Priority I 0, II 1, III 0, IV 0, V 1. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (10)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Gujarat: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 10 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Gujarat: Priority I 4, II 2, III 0, IV 2, V 2. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 4 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Haryana: Priority I 2, II 1, III 1, IV 0, V 0. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (10)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Jharkhand: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 10 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Jharkhand: Priority I 0, II 0, III 1, IV 1, V 8. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (14)

environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 14 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Karnataka: Priority I 3, II 0, III 4, IV 2, V 5. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (32)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Kerala: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 32 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Kerala: Priority I 0, II 0, III 2, IV 4, V 26. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (54)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Maharashtra: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 54 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Maharashtra: Priority I 2, II 5, III 9, IV 15, V 23. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 2 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Punjab: Priority I 2, II 0, III 0, IV 0, V 0. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 8 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Rajasthan: Priority I 0, II 0, III 0, IV 0, V 8. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

climate.name: State climate profile — climate types, rainfall and seasonal characteristics
climate.officialName: Climate of the North Eastern States
climate.classificationSystem: Köppen classification as interpreted in NEC Yearbook 2025
climateTypes: Cwb — subtropical highland at lower altitudes
BWk — cold desert on fringes of North Sikkim
BSk — cold semi-arid in parts of North Sikkim
Dwc — cool continental in parts of North Sikkim
Dwd — cold continental at higher altitudes
climate.sourceName: North Eastern Council Yearbook 2025; rainfall and climate references include IMD
climate.referenceDate: 2025 publication; normal periods vary by cited table
climate.description: Climate ranges from subtropical to alpine with elevation. Mean annual rainfall is about 2,548 mm, with nearly 64% during June–September; July is the wettest month. Average annual temperature is reported around 18°C, while northern areas are much cooler and can reach 0°C in winter. These are statewide summary descriptions; local climate varies with altitude and district. The source uses multiple reference periods, which should not be conflated.

soilTypes.sourceName: North Eastern Council Yearbook 2025; underlying ICAR-NBSS&LUP survey
soilTypes.description: The NEC Yearbook 2025 reports 3 soil orders, 7 sub-orders, 12 great groups and 26 sub-groups in this state. Soil-order shares of geographical area: entisols 42%; inceptisols 43%; mollisols 15%. Acidic soils are reported across 8% of the state area. These are survey-based statewide estimates, not current district-level soil maps.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (3)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Sikkim: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 3 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Sikkim: Priority I 0, II 2, III 0, IV 1, V 0. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (9)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Tamil Nadu: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 9 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Tamil Nadu: Priority I 5, II 1, III 0, IV 1, V 2. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.name: CPCB-identified polluted river locations and stretches (12)
environmentalChallenges.officialName: Uttarakhand: polluted river stretches and locations in CPCB 2025 assessment
environmentalChallenges.sourceName: Central Pollution Control Board — Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality, October 2025
environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 12 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for Uttarakhand: Priority I 5, II 0, III 4, IV 2, V 1. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

environmentalChallenges.description: CPCB's October 2025 assessment, based on river-water monitoring during 2022–2023, lists 11 polluted river stretches and/or single polluted river locations for West Bengal: Priority I 1, II 0, III 2, IV 2, V 6. The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.

The total combines multi-location polluted stretches with single monitoring locations; it is not a count of unique rivers or necessarily of separate stretches. Priority classes are based on maximum observed biochemical oxygen demand (BOD): I >30.1 mg/L; II 20.1–30.0; III 10.1–20.0; IV 6.1–10.0; V 3.1–6.0. A polluted segment does not mean the entire river is polluted.
